brief: Lane hr3: port the CUDA R3 batching speed work (rb3, #121) to HIP for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 on tatooine (R9700): (a) row tables, one launch per GDN/attention layer across rows, (b) HIP graphs per batch size, (c) extend the fused moe_block past T<=2 if it stays row-exact, (d) multi-row fp8/nvfp4 GEMVs only after profiling; device sampling stays opt-in; every batched row bitwise the solo step; single-stream speed within 1%. Baseline (main, --max-batch 16): 157.8 / 195.2 / 234.7 tok/s at 1 / 4 / 16 streams.
hypothesis: After hb the HIP batched step still issued one GDN conv, delta rule, KV append, rope, qk_norm and attention launch per row and per layer and ran eagerly; one row-table launch per op plus a graph per row count, and the fused MoE block at the 3 to 4 row steps that fall outside moe_block's T<=2, should lift 4 and 16 streams by 10% or more with every row still bitwise the solo step.

summary: R3 (a)+(b)+(c) ported to HIP and gated: row-table kernels for GDN conv/delta rule, KV append, rope and split-KV attention (one launch per op for all rows), a graph per row count (no new code, the generic path engages once no per-row launch is left), and the fused moe_block_bf16_rows at 3 and 4 rows (kernel row-exact to 16 rows, slower than the unfused chain above 4). 35B aggregate decode, 1k prompt, 3 bursts, same fleetq slot, main 6189466f as baseline: 1 stream 157.5 to 158.0, 4 streams 194.4 to 212.6 (+9.4%), 16 streams 231.8 to 257.1 (+10.9%), 4 streams with 4k prompts 141.2 to 145.3. A/B arms: row tables +6.9% (4x) and +10.9% (16x), graphs +3.3% and +0.9%, fused MoE block +4.5% at 4x. (d) was not touched: the fp8 GEMV is 25.8% of the B=16 step and a bitwise multi-row kernel is the next lever. Served throughput is 213 and 257 tok/s against 294 and 385 in the model-loop step test, so 5 to 20 ms per step sit outside the model step and were not profiled.
lessons: Tests run without admission; serve selects admitted kernels only. A row-table twin must take its base kernel's admission and plan::admit must not grade it with table-less cases, otherwise serve rejects or never selects it while every G-B and G-C test is green. Run serve and read the load line before believing a kernel PR.
rsync -a keeps edit times and cargo trusts a newer build: twice a 'final' binary was stale. Sync with --no-times --checksum and check the op list of the binary under test.

A fused kernel that reads each token's experts separately loses to the unfused chain that shares expert weights between rows once rows routed to the same expert multiply: moe_block_bf16_rows wins at 3 and 4 rows and loses +7% at 8 and +14% at 16, so the model caps it at 4.
A change that is 'inert with batching off' still moved a plan line (moe_block scratch 9216 to 18432 B) because solo two-row steps took the new path; the byte-identical plan show gate caught it.
Pick-check assertions in tests encode the old step shape (a MoeExperts rows kernel, an nvfp4 GEMV) and fail when a fusion replaces those calls; the numerical comparison had not failed.
